audit.why: Both layers and the packet agree on the shape: Jayce owns levels 1 through 5 while Mundo has no way to answer accelerated Shock Blast, and the lane turns at 6 and again at first item. The full layer's 8/10 and 7/10 early ratings match the prose. No change needed.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4].why for level 6 is champion-wide boilerplate ('six abilities against his four') and never names Maximum Dosage or says why the stage flips.
audit.why: Maximum Dosage is 120s flat and instantly heals a percentage of his MISSING health, then regenerates more over a long duration. _missing-interactions.json flags this pair for both needs-antiheal and resistances-invalidated. A generic level-6 line hides the one buy that decides the stage.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why rewritten around the missing-health heal and the anti-heal requirement.

audit.whatIsWrong: Goes Where He Pleases is never mentioned anywhere on the page. Every field treats Heart Zapper as the matchup-defining ability.
audit.why: Riot's passive text: Dr. Mundo resists the FIRST immobilising effect that hits him, losing health and dropping a chemical cannister instead, which he can walk over to restore health and reduce the passive's own cooldown. Against a Jayce whose whole peel plan is Thundering Blow, that is the single most important thing on the page — his answer to your first CC is built in, and the cannister he leaves behind is both his heal and your cue that the passive is now down.
audit.corrected: Stated in breakdown.cooldowns and the Key Ability Interactions entry.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns carried no numbers and named Heart Zapper as the thing to track, while the ability that actually governs the lane is Infected Bonesaw — 4 second cooldown, 975 range, current-health damage.
audit.why: 975 range out-reaches Jayce in Cannon form and a 4-second cooldown is not something you wait out. The page tells the player to poke from range against a champion who out-ranges his poke; the correct read is that Jayce wins on burst windows, not on a chip war.
audit.corrected: Real cooldowns and ranges for the passive, Q and W written into breakdown.cooldowns, report[5], and both dos/dont descriptions.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2] ('...wastes Heart Zapper') and dontsFull[1] carry descriptions copied from unrelated template lines, and dosFull[0].d repeats a fragment ('His sustain + reset. Anti-heal it.') that describes Heart Zapper's recast without saying what the recast does.
audit.why: Mismatched title/description pairs give no usable instruction.
audit.corrected: All three rewritten with real mechanics and numbers.

edits.before: - Dr. Mundo Heart Zapper: matchup-defining — His sustain + reset. Anti-heal it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Goes Where He Pleases (P): it eats the first immobilising effect outright, then he heals by walking onto the cannister. - Infected Bonesaw (Q), 4s, 975 range: current-health poke that out-ranges you. - Heart Zapper (W), 17s.

edits.before: Track Dr. Mundo's Heart Zapper: His sustain + reset. Anti-heal it. When it is down — Cannon-Q + hammer him.
edits.after: His passive eats your first immobilise and drops a cannister he heals off. Infected Bonesaw is 975 range at 4s.

edits.before: His sustain + reset. Anti-heal it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: His sustain plus the burst on recast. Anti-heal before you commit.

edits.before: Dr. Mundo wastes Heart Zapper — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Heart Zapper is 17s at rank 1 — that is your one clean window.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Infected Bonesaw is 975 range on a 4s timer — he out-pokes you.

edits.before: Form-swapping IS the ult — six abilities against his four. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Dr. Mundo's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Maximum Dosage heals a share of his missing health on a 120s timer, so armour and MR do nothing. Anti-heal or do not fight.

notes: One thing I deliberately did NOT write, because I could not verify it and it is exactly the kind of claim the brief warns about: whether Jayce's Thundering Blow knockback counts as an 'immobilising effect' for the purposes of Goes Where He Pleases. If it does, Mundo's passive eats Jayce's only peel tool and the correct advice is to bait the passive with something else first — which would be the single best line on this page. If it does not, the passive is far less relevant here. Riot's text says 'the first Immobilizing effect' without defining the category, displacements are often treated separately from immobilises, and champ-data/_kits/jayce.json leaves needsResearch empty. I wrote the passive's existence and its cannister-heal (both stated plainly by Riot) and stopped short of the interaction. This needs deciding before it ships. Also note MC_WR_TABLES.jayce lists drmundo at 44.37 while the packet reports 43.6 over 977 games — close, but the two disagree.
